content.thinking: I need to fix "within a minute" in CF-2 and change "continues through {G5309.3}" to "during {G5309.3}" instead. Checking other spots, the parenthetical ranges look fine as is, and "in the minute it was switched on" seems acceptable without a number attached.

action_items.item: Require tests that run each flag-guarded path of io-shop with its flag on, including edge-case accounts such as a shopper with no purchases this month, to pass before that flag can be switched on in production.
Switch io-shop feature flags on in stages, starting with a small share of requests, rather than for all traffic at once.
Halt a staged flag rollout on io-shop automatically, and switch the flag back off, when the account page error rate rises above its baseline.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account pages failed. The account page error rate the service logged reached {Gbac1.5}, against a typical {Gbac1.6}, and was highest at {Gbac1.7}. Across all requests the error rate was {errors_while_broken} while it was broken, against {errors_before} before.

Account page requests were failing with ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The service logged this error during {G5309.3}, from the onset on. Before the onset, the account page errors logged were shoppers closing the connection.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: the change events read over the wider window came back with only the two flag toggles and no deploy.

causal_chain.step: The failing code runs on the path that monthly-spend-feature enables, and an admin switched that flag on at {P1.1}. Every evaluation of the flag read off during {G7e5d.4}. At {G971b.6}, {G971b.2} of {G971b.3} evaluations read on, and every evaluation read on during {Gce95.4}. The failed revert does not clear the flag. The flag was switched off at {P2.1}, but the service kept logging the flag as on after that, so the switch-off was not seen to reach the service.

On the path the flag enables, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` builds the list of items bought this month and divides the month's total by the length of that list. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, the list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. The log names the same line.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on shoppers' account pages likely made the page divide by zero for shoppers who had bought before but nothing this month, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: Before monthly-spend-feature was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the path the flag enables against a shopper who had bought before but nothing this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have failed in the check, before the flag was switched on for shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for every account page request almost at once. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on a rise in errors was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of requests would have reached the failing path, and the rise in errors could have stopped the rollout before it reached all traffic.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to on-call paging, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been engaged once the alert was raised and could have seen that the service still logged the flag as on after it was switched off, rather than the incident ending with the flag back on.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well: The Investigator placed the onset at the same instant monthly-spend-feature was switched on, and named the failing line from the logs.
Argus switched off the flag that set it off {T19.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request for a person to review {T39.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: The revert was judged refuted while the service's own log lines still showed monthly-spend-feature evaluated as on after the switch-off. The flag was put back on, and the incident ended with the triggering change still in place.
Argus's memory held an earlier incident in which the same flag revert had been refuted. The revert was tried again without first checking whether such a switch-off reaches the service.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of items bought this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division at line {F1.1} raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: With monthly-spend-feature back on and the division unchanged, account pages for shoppers who bought nothing this month would likely keep failing.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at io-shop itself that its flag-evaluation log lines read monthly-spend-feature=off and that the ZeroDivisionError lines at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stop: after the earlier switch-off, the service's lines still read on.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out why io-shop kept logging monthly-spend-feature as on after the flag provider switched it off at {P2.1}, and whether that switch-off ever reached the service's flag evaluation. If it did reach it, find out why account page requests kept failing.
